findings.evidence: Line 81-83: `@[expose] def resFDRep ... := (Action.res (FGModuleCat k) S.subtype).obj B`; lemmas resFDRep_ρ (87), character_resFDRep (93), forget₂_obj_resFDRep (98) all `:= rfl` supply the full interface; indFDRep at FiniteDimensional.lean:259 is opaque with a bridge iso.
findings.fix: Drop @[expose] from resFDRep; keep the three characteristic lemmas as the interface. If any rfl-lemma then needs the body sealed, prove it with `:= (rfl)` instead of `:= rfl` per the repo idiom (cf. characterPairing_apply).
findings.issue: resFDRep is marked @[expose], exposing its body `(Action.res (FGModuleCat k) S.subtype).obj B` to importers. The complete characteristic API already exists as rfl-lemmas (resFDRep_ρ, character_resFDRep, forget₂_obj_resFDRep), so no consumer needs the body: the in-file defeq compositions in indResFDRepHomEquiv/resIndFDRepHomEquiv hold in-module regardless of @[expose], which only governs cross-module visibility. Exposing the body couples downstream proofs to the Action.res implementation. This is inconsistent with the sibling indFDRep (FiniteDimensional.lean:259), kept opaque behind indFDRepForgetIso.

summary: The exposed surface, characteristic API, and simp annotations are otherwise correct and match the roadmap signatures, but resFDRep carries a needless @[expose] that leaks its implementation body.
